content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 10
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 16

---

## V.3 — "presentation of the bread" vs. "bread of presentation" vs. "sacred bread"
- EMET: "presentation of the bread"
- LOGOS: "bread of presentation"
- PNEUMA: "the sacred bread" (loses the technical liturgical term)
- SOPHIA: "bread of presentation" — technical term *prothesis* should be preserved

## V.4 — "begged the Lord" vs. "implored the Lord" vs. "begged the Lord"
- EMET/PNEUMA: "begged"
- LOGOS: "implored"
- SOPHIA: "implored" — slightly more formal for prostrate supplication

## V.4 — "forbearance" vs. "clemency" vs. "mercy"
- EMET: "forbearance"
- LOGOS: "clemency"
- PNEUMA: "mercy"
- SOPHIA: "clemency" — Greek *epieikeia*: fairness, reasonableness; "clemency" captures the judicial/punitive context best

## V.6 — "Feast of Tabernacles" vs. "Festival of Booths" vs. "Festival of Booths"
- EMET: "Feast of Tabernacles"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "Festival of Booths"
- SOPHIA: "Festival of Booths" — modern standard rendering preferred

## V.7 — "offered hymns of thanksgiving" vs. "offered hymns of thanksgiving" vs. "sang hymns of praise"
- EMET/LOGOS: "offered hymns of thanksgiving"
- PNEUMA: "sang hymns of praise"
- SOPHIA: "offered hymns of thanksgiving" — Greek *hymnous prospherontes*: bringing/offering hymns; retain the offering/presentation language

## V.8 — PNEUMA adds parenthetical "(This is the origin of Hanukkah)"
- Not in Greek text
- SOPHIA: omit; the note is helpful but editorially inappropriate for a translation

## V.9 — Chapter transition placement
- EMET/LOGOS: brief transition sentence about Antiochus
- PNEUMA: same but adds "That was how..." as a conclusive phrasing
- SOPHIA: "Such was the end of Antiochus" — EMET/LOGOS reading

## V.13 — "no honorable way out" vs. "no honorable way of extricating himself" vs. "no way out and no way to reclaim his honor"
- EMET: "no honorable way out"
- LOGOS: "no honorable way of extricating himself"
- PNEUMA: expands significantly
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — captures Greek *euschemon exodon* (honorable exit)

## V.18 — "nine thousand fled into" vs. "nine thousand had taken refuge in" vs. "nine thousand more had taken refuge in"
- EMET: "fled into"
- LOGOS: "had taken refuge in"
- PNEUMA: "had taken refuge in" with "more"
- SOPHIA: "had fled into" — Greek *katephugon*: fled for refuge; simple verb preferred

## V.20 — "money-lovers" vs. "lovers of money" vs. "greedy"
- EMET: "money-lovers" (compound)
- LOGOS: "lovers of money"
- PNEUMA: "greedy" (loses the Greek compound *philargyria*)
- SOPHIA: "lovers of money" — Greek *philargyros*; retain compound sense

## V.25 — "girded their loins with sackcloth" vs. "bound their loins with sackcloth" vs. "wrapped themselves in sackcloth"
- EMET: "girded"
- LOGOS: "bound"
- PNEUMA: "wrapped" (less precise)
- SOPHIA: "girded their loins with sackcloth" — traditional and accurate

## V.27 — "retreat to the Lord as their refuge" vs. "recourse to the Lord as their refuge" vs. "the Lord as their refuge"
- EMET: "retreat to the Lord as their refuge"
- LOGOS: "recourse to the Lord as their refuge"
- PNEUMA: "the Lord as their refuge" (simplified)
- SOPHIA: "their recourse to the Lord as their refuge" — LOGOS preferred

## V.28 — "resplendent men" vs. "magnificent men" vs. "magnificent horsemen"
- EMET: "resplendent men on horses"
- LOGOS: "magnificent men on horseback"
- PNEUMA: "magnificent horsemen"
- SOPHIA: "five magnificent men on horseback" — LOGOS phrasing

## V.29 — "hurling arrows and thunderbolts" vs. "hurling arrows and thunderbolts" vs. "pouring arrows and lightning bolts"
- PNEUMA: "pouring" (less vivid) and "lightning bolts" (acceptable synonym)
- SOPHIA: "hurling arrows and thunderbolts" — EMET/LOGOS

## V.36 — "pit" vs. "cistern" vs. "pit"
- EMET/PNEUMA: "pit"
- LOGOS: "cistern"
- SOPHIA: "cistern" — Greek *lakkon*: cistern or pit; "cistern" more precise in a military fortress context

## V.38 — "great benefits" vs. "great benefits" vs. "pours out his blessings"
- EMET/LOGOS: "great benefits" (Greek *megaleia*)
- PNEUMA: "pours out his blessings" (interpretive)
- SOPHIA: "great benefits" retained
